newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian refinery may restrict sale volumes.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian refinery may restrict sale volumes.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim may restrict the refined oil product volumes it sells to traders and distributors to prevent stockpiling, a refinery official said on Thursday.

"There is again a long queue of trucks at the refinery's terminal as a result of a panic over a new fuel price hike, which indicates that traders are stockpiling the fuel," a Neftohim official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
Since the end of November Bulgaria has been suffering from petrol and diesel shortages as suppliers hold back products in expectation of price rises.

"It is a normal reaction of traders and recently producers to try to hold back some volumes when a price hike is expected and to sell them at a better price on the following day," the executive director of the country's biggest fuel retailer Bedo Doganian said in a television interview on Wednesday.
"In the meantime Neftohim is suffering serious losses," he said, adding that price and tax inspectors were now exercising strict control on filling stations and fuel storages.
On Monday the government unexpectedly announced a new rise in petrol prices by an average 21 percent and diesel prices by 26 percent following a previous rise on November 28.
The cabinet usually revises energy prices each month in line with inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.
The refinery is pressing the government for more frequent revisions of the fuel prices because of the rapid slide of the lev against the dollar, officials said.
Current crude prices were based on a rate of 260 levs per dollar while Neftohim is now buying at almost double that price, Neftohim executive director Stefan Nedelchev said this week.
The lev traded at 530-540 per dollar on the interbank foreign exchange market on Thursday, compared to 355 on November 28.
Energy officials said the Neftohim refinery was a bitter example of how a gap between low local fuel prices and high production costs was turning a profitable firm into a debt-ridden one.
Neftohim's spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said the refinery sold 3,200 tonnes of products on Wednesday, which "is more than the usual volumes for the (winter) season".
The plant now produces 20,000 tonnes of petrol per day from 18,000 tonnes at the beginning of December, Hadzhieva said.

A 70,000-tonne tanker is being unloaded at the Bourgas port and three other tankers were waiting for loading with crude for the Bourgas refinery at Russia's Novorosiisk Black Sea port, Hadzhieva said.
